reason: A proxy that checks limits, routes big actions to a human and has a kill switch is something my team can build in a quarter, and I'm not putting an unaudited startup with no customers inline on every trade. Even the free design partnership asks me for a reference and a letter of intent naming a price, and I'm not signing either for a vendor I'd be explaining to my examiner.
objection: The identity check depends on AINRA passports, and the founder of the vendor started that registry. If the gate in front of my order flow trusts a registry its own founder controls, that conflict is the first thing an examiner will ask about, and I have no good answer.
would_change_my_mind: AINRA, or whatever Know-Your-Agent standard they check, being run independently of the vendor and adopted by other venues, plus a finished SOC 2 Type II. Then the registry and the exam-ready evidence export would be the parts I can't build myself.
